rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Paradise, Adam would not become thirsty.
rows.anchor: { وأنك لا تظمأ فيها } يعنى لا تعطش فى الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun's heat would not afflict and harm him there.
rows.anchor: فى الجنة { ولا تضحى } [آية: 119] يقول: لا يصيبك حر الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tempter was Iblis alone, who offered Adam a tree of immortality and a kingdom that would not perish.
rows.anchor: { فوسوس إليه الشيطان } يعنى إبليس وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever ate from the tree would live eternally in Paradise and not die.
rows.anchor: من أكل منها خلد فى الجنة فلا يموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised kingdom was one that would not pass away.
rows.anchor: على { وملك لا يبلى } [آية: 120] يقول: لا يفنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After they ate, their nakedness became visible.
rows.anchor: { فأكلا منها فبدت لهما سوءاتهما } يقول: ظهرت لهما عوراتهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They stuck leaves together, using fig leaves from Paradise to cover themselves.
rows.anchor: { وطفقا يخصفان عليهما } يقول: وجعلا يخصفان، يقول: يلزقان الورق بعضه على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam strayed and turned away from obeying his Lord.
rows.anchor: يعنى فضل وتولى عن طاعة ربه، عز وجل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His Lord selected and drew Adam close.
rows.anchor: { ثم اجتباه ربه } يعنى استخلصه ربه عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepted Adam's repentance for his sin and guided him to repent.
rows.anchor: يعنى استخلصه ربه عز وجل { فتاب عليه } من ذنبه { وهدى } [آية: 122] يعنى وهداه للتوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two commanded to descend are Adam and Iblis.
rows.anchor: { قال اهبطا منها جميعا } يعنى آدم وإبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis and his descendants are enemies of Adam and his descendants.
rows.anchor: { بعضكم لبعض عدو } يقول: إبليس وذريته عدو لآدم وذريته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guidance comes through messengers bearing books that contain clarification.
rows.anchor: يعنى رسلا معهم كتب فيها البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following God's guidance means following His messengers and His book.
rows.anchor: { فمن اتبع هداي } يعنى رسلى وكتابى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The follower will not go astray in this world or suffer in the next.
rows.anchor: { فلا يضل } فى الدنيا { ولا يشقى } [آية: 123] فى الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away from remembrance means refusing belief in the Qur'an; the warning was revealed about al-Aswad b. Abd al-Aswad al-Makhzumi, whom Hamza killed at Badr by the watering place.
rows.anchor: نزلت فى الأسود بن عبد الأسود المخزومى، قتله حمزة بن عبد المطلب يوم بدر على الحوض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A constricted life is an evil life, constricted because it is spent disobeying God.
rows.anchor: { فإن له معيشة ضنكا } يعنى معيشة سوء لأنها فى معاصى الله عز وجل الضنك والضيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person is gathered blind with respect to his argument or proof.
rows.anchor: أعمى } [آية: 124] عن حجته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker is blind to his proof, although he knew it in worldly life.
rows.anchor: هلك عني سلطانيه [الحاقة: 29] يعنى ضلت عنى حجتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links the lost proof to 69:29, interpreting it as my proof has gone from me.
rows.anchor: هلك عني سلطانيه [الحاقة: 29] يعنى ضلت عنى حجتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is said when the person's limbs testify against him for associating partners with God and disbelief.
rows.anchor: وهذا قوله حين شهدت عليه الجوارح بالشرك والكفر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs that came to him were the Qur'an's signs.
rows.anchor: { أتتك آياتنا } يعنى آيات القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting here means abandoning belief in the Qur'anic signs.
rows.anchor: { فنسيتها } يعنى فتركت إيمانا بآيات القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the afterlife he is left in the Fire, never taken out and no longer remembered by God.
rows.anchor: { وكذلك اليوم تنسى } [آية: 126] فى الآخرة تترك فى النار، ولا تخرج منها، ولا نذكرك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The profligate meant here is one who associated partners with God in this life.
rows.anchor: { وكذلك نجزي من أسرف } يعنى وهكذا نجزى من أشرك فى الدنيا بالنار فى الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's signs are the Qur'an, which the disbeliever did not believe.
rows.anchor: { ولم يؤمن بآيات ربه } يقول: ولم يؤمن بالقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife punishment is worse than the worldly punishment of being killed at Badr and lasts longer; this warns Meccan unbelievers.
rows.anchor: { ولعذاب الآخرة أشد } مما أصابه فى الدنيا من القتل ببدر { وأبقى } [آية: 127] يعنى وأدوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers are Meccan unbelievers asking for a sign to show Muhammad is a prophet and messenger, as signs came to earlier prophets and their peoples.
rows.anchor: { وقالوا } أى كفار مكة: { لولا } يعنى هلا { يأتينا بآية من ربه

words: أَوَلَمْ تَأْتِهِم بَيِّنَةُ مَا فِى ٱلصُّحُفِ ٱلْأُولَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear proof is the explanation in the books of Abraham and Moses, which preceded Muhammad's book.
rows.anchor: { أولم تأتهم بينة ما في الصحف الأولى } [آية: 133] يعنى بيان كتب إبراهيم وموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God had destroyed them with punishment in this world before the Qur'an came in the afterlife, they would have objected that no messenger with a book had been sent.
rows.anchor: { ولو أنآ أهلكناهم بعذاب } فى الدنيا { من قبله } يعنى من قبل هذا القرآن فى الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being humbled means being made low; being disgraced means being punished in this world.
rows.anchor: { من قبل أن نذل } يعنى نستذل { ونخزى } [آية: 134] يعنى ونعذب فى الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccan unbelievers awaited Muhammad's death, while Muhammad awaited the worldly punishment he had threatened them with.
rows.anchor: كفار مكة، قالوا: نتربص بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، الموت لأن النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم، أوعدهم العذاب فى الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands the Meccans to wait as they do, while Muhammad waits for their worldly punishment to descend.
rows.anchor: { قل } لكفار مكة { كل متربص } أنتم بمحمد الموت، ومحمد يتربص بكم العذاب فى الدنيا

words: فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ أَصْحَٰبُ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ ٱلسَّوِىِّ وَمَنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is justice; the question is which side, us or you, is rightly guided.
rows.anchor: من أصحاب الصراط السوى } يعني العدل أنحن أم أنتم { ومن اهتدى } [آية: 135] منا ومنكم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: On the replacement described in 18:81, the Prophet reportedly said that a boy was born to them afterward.
rows.anchor: عن أبى بن كعب، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فى قوله عز وجل: ... خيرا منه زكاة وأقرب رحما

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: At their parting, Khidr told Moses that patience would have let him witness a thousand marvels beyond those he had seen; Moses wept at leaving him.
rows.anchor: عن حذيفة، أنه لما حان للخضر وموسى، عليهما السلام، أن يفترقا

rows.speaker: الخضر
rows.claim: Khidr advised Moses to focus on the afterlife, avoid pointless matters, remember fear and hope in changing circumstances, do good while able, and consider outcomes.
rows.anchor: قال له الخضر: يا موسى، اجعل همك فى معادك، ولا تخض فيما لا يعينك

rows.speaker: الخضر
rows.claim: Khidr further warned Moses against self-admiration, wasting his remaining life, and forgetting that God never neglects him.
rows.anchor: قال له الخضر: إياك والإعجاب بنفسك، والتفريط فيما بقى من عمرك

rows.speaker: الخضر
rows.claim: Khidr warned against stubbornness, unnecessary journeys and pointless laughter, and against shaming repentant sinners; one should weep over one's own sin.
rows.anchor: قال له الخضر: إياك واللجاجة، ولا تمش فى غير حاجة، ولا تضحك من غير عجب

rows.speaker: موسى
rows.claim: Moses told Khidr to be angry only for God, to approve, love, and hate only for God, and warned that worldly love or hatred can lead out of faith into disbelief.
rows.anchor: قال له موسى: إياك والغضب إلا فى الله تعالى، ولا ترض عن أحد إلا فى الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses and Khidr watched a bird skim the sea and dip its beak twice; Khidr said he could not explain its loss unless God enabled him.
rows.anchor: إذ انقضت خطافة فنقرت بمنقارها من البحر نقرتين.

rows.speaker: الخضر
rows.claim: Khidr said every thing has blessing except people's lifespans and allotted terms; without this limit, people would perish, since what is depleted without replenishment runs out.
rows.anchor: قال له الخضر: نعم يا موسى، ما من شىء إلا وفيه بركة ما خلا آجال العباد

rows.speaker: الخضر
rows.claim: Asked about his exceptional knowledge and lifespan, Khidr attributed them to abstaining from sin, thanking God, keeping a sound heart, and fearing and hoping in God alone.
rows.anchor: قال له الخضر: يا موسى، بالصبر عن معصية الله، عز وجل، والشكر لله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas said the parents were given a girl in place of the boy.
rows.anchor:
سمعت ابن عباس على المنبر يقول:
فأردنآ أن يبدلهما ربهما خيرا منه زكاة وأقرب رحما
[الكهف: 81]، قال: جارية مكان الغلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas said the treasure was a gold tablet bearing the basmala, the testimony that God alone is God and Ahmad is His messenger, and maxims about fate, death, and the world's instability.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، فى قوله عز وجل: {... وكان تحته كنز لهما... } قال: كان لوحا من ذهب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas said Khidr had not forgotten; the expression was an instance of indirect or equivocal speech.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، فى قوله عز وجل:

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali said the Turks were a band from Gog and Magog that raided people; Dhul-Qarnayn blocked them behind the barrier, where they remained.
rows.anchor: عن على، رضى الله عنه، وقد لقيه، قال: إن الترك سرية خرجوا من يأجوج ومأجوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil explains the name Turks as meaning those left behind the barrier.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: إنما سموا الترك؛ لأنهم تركوا خلف الردم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A king asked Dhul-Qarnayn about four pairs: the standing heavens and earth, moving sun and moon, day and night sharing time, and mutually opposed death and life; the king accepted his answer as learned.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: انتهى ذو القرنين إلى ملك من ملوك الأرض

rows.speaker: مطرف بن الشخير
rows.claim: Mutarrif b. al-Shikhkhir said knowledge is better than abundant action, the best action is moderate, and a good deed lies between two bad ones; he illustrated this with 17:110.
rows.anchor: عن عون بن عبد الله المزنى، عن مطرف بن الشخير، أنه قال: فضل العلم خير من فضل العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil derives Adam's name from the earth's surface, Hawwa's from a living being, Noah's from lamenting, and Abraham's from being father of nations or a merciful father.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: تفسير آدم، عليه السلام، لأنه خلق من أديم الأرض، وتفسير حواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil explains Isaac's name by Sarah's laughter, Jacob's by grasping Esau's heel in the womb, and Joseph's as an increase in beauty.
rows.anchor: وتفسير إسحاق لضحك سارة، ويعقوب لأنه خرج من بطن أمه قابض على عقب العيص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil explains Yahya's name as revived or brought to life between two elderly parents, a very old man and a barren woman.
rows.anchor: وتفسير يحيى: أحيى من بين ميتين، لأنه خرج من بين شيخ كبير، وعجوز عاقر

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a dream, Gabriel told the Prophet that God granted him his whole community on Judgment Day and would grant others if he asked; the Prophet rejoiced.
rows.anchor: دخل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على ابنة عمته أم هانىء فنعس، فوضعت له وسادة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In another dream, Gabriel told the Prophet that Paradise longed for him and his community, which made him laugh joyfully.
rows.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على ابنة عمته أم هانىء فنعس، فوضعت له وسادة، فوضع رأسه فنام، بينما هو نائم إذ ضحك

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a third dream the Prophet saw his community carrying rods of light that illuminated the distance between east and west; Gabriel identified them as Islam.
rows.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على ابنة عمته أم هانىء فنعس، فوضعت له وسادة، فوضع رأسه فنام، بينما هو نائم إذ ضحك

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet saw Paradise's pearl and ruby palaces and was told they were for him and his community, adorned two thousand years before his creation.
rows.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على ابنة عمته أم هانىء فنعس، فوضعت له وسادة، فوضع رأسه فنام، بينما هو نائم إذ ضحك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet said Firdaws was created and planted by God's hand, incomparable to anything seen or imagined, then commanded to adorn itself twice and speak; it declared that the believers prospered.
rows.anchor:
عن مقاتل، عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" لما خلق الله عز وجل جنة الفردوس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet's report says Firdaws named the successful as the monotheists of Muhammad's community, who inherit Firdaws eternally.
rows.anchor:
عن مقاتل، عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" لما خلق الله عز وجل جنة الفردوس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The report says Firdaws's gate stays closed until Resurrection, its fragrance and houris are at its entrance, and the Prophet waits at the Pool to turn away unbelievers and recognize his community by ablution's light.
rows.anchor:
عن مقاتل، عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" لما خلق الله عز وجل جنة الفردوس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet said whoever drinks from his Pool will never thirst again; Muadh called such drinkers fortunate, and the Prophet said a monotheist who believes in the messenger drinks and enters Firdaws.
rows.anchor:
عن مقاتل، عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" لما خلق الله عز وجل جنة الفردوس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet told Muadh that those who die Muslim were created Muslim in Adam, passed through unbelieving ancestors until they believed in him, and are his brothers, while his contemporaries are his companions.
rows.anchor:
عن مقاتل، عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" لما خلق الله عز وجل جنة الفردوس

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet followed his account of the believers as his brothers by reciting 15:47, on brothers seated facing one another.
rows.anchor: ثم قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إخوانا على سرر متقابلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The firm mountains are embedded in the earth to anchor it and keep it from swaying or shifting.
rows.anchor: { وجعلنا في الأرض رواسي } يعنى الجبال أرسيت فى الأرض، فأثبتت الأرض بالجبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fajjas are mountain passes or valleys made into roads so people can find their way.
rows.anchor: { فجاجا } يعنى كل شعب فى جبل فيه منذ { سبلا } يعنى طرقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is a raised roof, protected from devils so they cannot overhear the angels and tell people what they hear.
rows.anchor: { وجعلنا السمآء سقفا } يعنى المرفوع { محفوظا } من الشياطين لئلا يسمعوا إلى كلام الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs include the sun, moon, stars, and other celestial signs; people ignore them instead of reflecting on God's handiwork and affirming His oneness.
rows.anchor: يعنى الشمس والقمر والنجوم وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon enter from the west, pass beneath the earth to the east, then travel through the sky to the west; falak means orbit and yasbahun means run, describing their circuit.
rows.anchor: { يسبحون } يعنى يجرون، فذلك دورانهما

words: قَالَ أَفَتَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنفَعُكُمْ شَيْـًۭٔا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim asks why they worship idols that cannot benefit them if worshipped or harm them if left unworshipped.
rows.anchor: إن عبدتموهم { ولا يضركم } [آية: 66] إن لم تعبدوهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uff is a reproachful or bad expression, spoken against them and the idols they worship.
rows.anchor: { أف لكم } يعنى بقوله: أف لكم، الكلام الردئ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim asks them to reason that the idols are not gods.
rows.anchor: { تعقلون } [آية: 67] أنها ليست بآلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They decided to burn Ibrahim; telling them to help their gods means exacting revenge for them.
rows.anchor: { قالوا حرقوه } بالنار { وانصروا آلهتكم } يقول: انتقموا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire was made cool in respect of its heat.
rows.anchor: { قلنا ينار كوني بردا } من الحر { وسلاما على إبراهيم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire was made safe from cold for Ibrahim; without the added safety, its chill would have killed him.
rows.anchor: ولو لم يقل: وسلاما، لأهلكه بردها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Ibrahim emerged, people hurried to inform Nimrod but could not understand one another; God confused their tongues into seventy languages, which explains the name Babylon.
rows.anchor: فبلبل الله ألسنتهم على سبعين لغة، فمن ثم سميت بابل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God barred them from reaching Ibrahim and made them the greatest losers.
rows.anchor: وحجزهم الله عنه { فجعلناهم الأخسرين } [آية: 70].

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Job called on God, saying that affliction had struck him and that God is the most merciful.
rows.anchor: { وأيوب إذ نادى ربه } يعنى دعاء ربه، عز وجل، { أني مسني الضر } يعنى أصابنى البلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answered Job's supplication and removed his affliction.
rows.anchor: { فاستجبنا له } دعاءه { فكشفنا ما به من ضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Job's wife had borne seven sons and three daughters before his trial; God revived them and gave him as many again, doubling everything he had lost.
rows.anchor: وكانت امرأة أيوب ولدت قبل البلاء سبع بنين وثلاث بنات، فأحياهم الله، عز وجل، ومثلهم معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mercy is a blessing, and the event is a reminder or reflection for monotheists.
rows.anchor: يقول: نعمة { من عندنا وذكرى للعابدين } [آية: 84] يقول: وتفكرا للموحدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Job was among the most devout people; Iblis tried to make him abandon worship of God but could not.
rows.anchor: وكان أيوب من أعبد الناس فجهد إبليس ليزيله عن عبادة ربه، عز وجل، فلم يستطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ismail, Idris, and Dhul-Kifl are the patient ones named here.
rows.anchor: { وإسماعيل وإدريس وذا الكفل كل من الصابرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being brought into God's mercy means receiving His blessing, namely prophethood; they were believers and righteous.
rows.anchor: يعنى فى نعمتنا وهى النبوة { إنهم من الصالحين } [آية: 86] يعنى من المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man of the fish is Jonah, son of Matta.
rows.anchor: { وذا النون } يعنى يونس بن متى، عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah left in defiance of his people, Hizqil b. Ajar and the Israelites with him, departing before they believed.
rows.anchor: { إذ ذهب مغاضبا } يعنى مراغما لقومه، لحزقيل بن أجار، ومن معه من بنى إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah supposed God would not punish him for what he had done.
rows.anchor: فحسب يونس أن لن نعاقبه بما صنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three darknesses are night, the sea, and the whale's belly.
rows.anchor: ظلمات ثلاث ظلمة الليل، وظلمة البحر، وظلمة بطن الحوت

words: أَن لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah affirmed God's oneness and declared Him free of having wronged Jonah.
rows.anchor: { أن لا إله إلا أنت } يوحد ربه، عز وجل: { سبحانك } نزه تعالى أن يكون ظلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah acknowledged that he had wronged himself.
rows.anchor: يقول يونس عليه السلام: إنى ظلمت نفسى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answered Jonah's supplication and rescued him from the whale's belly; God similarly rescues believers.
rows.anchor: { فاستجبنا له } دعاءه { ونجيناه من الغم } يعنى من بطن الحوت { وكذلك ننجي المؤمنين }

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra, as quoted by Tha'lab, says both forms carry the same sense, from measuring or apportioning, not from having power over someone.
rows.anchor: قال أبو العباس ثعلب: قال الفراء: أن لن نقدر عليه. ونقدر عليه، لمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The usage is compared with 89:16, where constricting provision derives from allotment or restriction rather than inability.
rows.anchor:
ومثله فى سورة الفجر:
فقدر عليه رزقه
[الفجر: 16]
من التقدير، والتقتير، لا من القدرة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says Jonah remained in the whale's belly for three days.
rows.anchor:
بلغنا أن النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:
" مكث يونس، عليه السلام، فى بطن الحوت

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Ka'b said Jonah remained in the whale's belly for forty days.
rows.anchor: وعن كعب قال: أربعين يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The simile is of a sheet or scroll containing writing being folded up.
rows.anchor: { يوم نطوي السمآء كطي السجل للكتب } يعنى كطى الصحيفة فيها الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccans swore in 16:38 that God would not raise the dead; God refutes them and promises to recreate people in the afterlife as He created them in worldly life.
rows.anchor:
فى سورة النحل:
... لا يبعث الله من يموت...
[النحل: 38]، فأكذبهم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Re-creation is a binding promise from God that He will carry out.
rows.anchor: { وعدا علينآ إنا كنا فاعلين } [آية: 104]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies the scriptures called Zabur here as the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms; al-dhikr is the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: { ولقد كتبنا في الزبور } يعنى التوراة والإنجيل والزبور { من بعد الذكر } يعنى اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth belongs to God and His righteous servants who inherit it are the believers.
rows.anchor: لله { يرثها عبادي الصالحون } [آية: 105] يعنى المؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is a conveyance to Paradise for worshippers, meaning monotheists.
rows.anchor: القرآن { لبلاغا } إلى الجنة { لقوم عابدين } [آية: 106] يعنى موحدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's sacred prohibitions here mean all the rites of pilgrimage; honoring them benefits a person in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: يعنى أمر المناسك كلها { فهو خير له عند ربه } فى الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The livestock made lawful are the animals that polytheists had dedicated to idols, as discussed in 6:138.
rows.anchor: بهيمة { الأنعام } التى حرموا للآلهة فى سورة الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception points to the prohibitions recited at the beginning of 5:3.
rows.anchor: { إلا ما يتلى عليكم } من التحريم فى أول سورة المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase has fronting and means to avoid worshipping the idols Lat, Uzza, and Manat.
rows.anchor: { فاجتنبوا الرجس من الأوثان } فيها تقديم يقول: اتقوا عبادة اللات والعزى ومناة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: False speech means lying, which is shirk.
rows.anchor: { واجتنبوا قول الزور } [آية: 30] يقول: اتقوا الكذب، وهو الشرك

rows.speaker: محمد بن على
rows.claim: Muhammad b. Ali explains false speech as the polytheistic talbiya of Quraysh, Khuza'a, Kinana, and Amir b. Sa'sa'a, who excepted a partner owned by God and meant the angels they worshipped.
rows.anchor: عن مقاتل، عن محمد بن على، فى قوله تعالى: { واجتنبوا قول الزور } قال: الكذب وهو الشرك فى التلبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In pre-Islamic pilgrimage, Yemenites called themselves the servants of Akk and asked to make pilgrimage again on riding camels.
rows.anchor: وكان أهل اليمن فى الجاهلية يقولون فى التلبية: نحن عرابا عك عك إليك عانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamim's talbiya mentioned the day's toil, night travel, cold, and heat, saying it did not avoid or harm anything and that the pilgrimage was for a generous Lord.
rows.anchor: وكانت تميم تقول في إحرامها: لبيك ما نهارنا نجره، إدلاجه وبرده وحره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabi'a declared a true pilgrimage in worship and servitude, denying that they came for mourning or profit.
rows.anchor: لم نأتك للمناحة، ولا حبا للرباحة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qays Aylan's talbiya included an appeal framed around Bakr and the Banu Aghyar.
rows.anchor: وكانت قيس عيلان تقول: لبيك لولا أن بكرا دونكا، بنو أغيار وهم يلونكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurhum's talbiya claimed they were God's servants and ancient stock, had settled His land, were first to keep His covenant, opposed His enemies, and would uphold religion in the valley.
rows.anchor: والناس طرف وهم تلادك، وهم لعمرى عمروا بلادك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quda'a invoked God as Lord of the sacred and unrestricted territories and asked for mercy as its people came walking.
rows.anchor: ارحم مقام عبد وآم، أتوك يمشون على الأقدام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asad and Ghatafan used a Yemeni-style chant about a camel running toward God, its load and unborn foal, and opposition to Christianity.
rows.anchor: وكانت أسد وغطفان تقول فى إحرامها بشعر اليمن: لبيك، إليك تعدوا قلقا وضينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some women circled the Kaaba naked at night; another account says they did so by day wearing only the edge of a garment and reciting a verse about exposed parts and gazing on them.
rows.anchor: وكانت النساء تطفن بالليل عراة، وقال بعضهم: لا بل نهارا تأخذ إحداهن حاشية برد

rows.speaker: آدم
rows.claim: Adam's talbiya said he was God's servant, created by God's hands, honored and brought near, and affirmed God as Lord of the House.
rows.anchor: وكانت تلبية آدم، عليه السلام: لبيك الله لبيك عبد خلقته بيديك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to avoid false speech means to avoid lying and the shirk uttered during ihram.
rows.anchor: فأنزل الله عز وجل: { واجتنبوا قول الزور } يعنى الكذب، وهو الشرك فى الإحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers have prospered, meaning they have become happy; believers here are those who affirm God's oneness.
rows.anchor: { قد أفلح المؤمنون } [آية: 1] يعنى سعد المؤمنون، يعنى المصدقين بتوحيد الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humility in prayer means submission: the praying person does not notice who is to his right or left.
rows.anchor: { الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون } [آية: 2] يقول: متواضعون يعنى إذا صلى لم يعرف من عن يمينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Vain talk means insults and harm from Meccan unbelievers against Muslims for accepting Islam; the phrase is connected to 25:72.
rows.anchor: يعنى اللغو: الشتم والأذى إذا سمعوه من كفار مكة لإسلامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doing zakah means paying the zakah due on their wealth.
rows.anchor: { والذين هم للزكاة فاعلون } [آية: 4] يعنى زكاة أموالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guarding private parts means refraining from indecencies, subject to the lawful exceptions that follow.
rows.anchor: { والذين هم لفروجهم حافظون } [آية: 5] عن الفواحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sexual relations with wives and female slaves are permitted; one is not blameworthy for lawful relations.
rows.anchor: { إلا على أزواجهم } يعنى حلائلهم { أو ما ملكت أيمانهم } من الولائد { فإنهم غير ملومين } [آية: 6]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone who seeks sexual indecencies beyond what is lawful is a transgressor.
rows.anchor: { فمن ابتغى وراء ذلك فأولئك هم العادون } [آية: 7] يقول: فمن ابتغى الفواحش بعد الحلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They preserve the performance of trusts and fulfill their covenants.
rows.anchor: يقول: يحافظون على أداء الأمانة، ووفاء العهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preserving the prayers means observing their appointed times.
rows.anchor: { والذين هم على صلواتهم يحافظون } [آية: 9] على المواقيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers described above are the inheritors.
rows.anchor: ثم أخبر بثوابهم، فقال: { أولئك هم الوارثون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Firdaws is a walled garden; the word is Roman in origin.
rows.anchor: الذين يرثون الفردوس } يعنى البستان عليه الحيطان، بالرومية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They remain in Paradise forever and do not die.
rows.anchor: { هم فيها خالدون } [آية: 11] يعنى فى الجنة لا يموتون

words: ثُمَّ أَنشَأْنَا مِنۢ بَعْدِهِمْ قَرْنًا ءَاخَرِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The new generation after Noah's people is the people of Hud.
rows.anchor: { ثم أنشأنا } يعنى قوم هود، عليه السلام، { من بعدهم } يعنى من بعد قوم نوح { قرنا آخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger was one of their own people; worshipping God means affirming His oneness, since He alone is their Lord.
rows.anchor: { فأرسلنا فيهم رسولا منهم } يعنى من أنفسهم { أن اعبدوا الله } يعنى أن وحدوا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to fear God means asking why they do not worship Him.
rows.anchor: يعنى أفهلا تعبدون الله، عز وجل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The malaʾ are the chiefs or prominent members of the people.
rows.anchor: { وقال الملأ } يعنى الأشراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs rejected God's oneness and denied resurrection, where deeds would be repaid; they had been made prosperous in worldly life.
rows.anchor: يعنى بالبعث الذى فيه جزاء الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs mean Hud is merely a human like them and has no superiority; he eats and drinks as they do.
rows.anchor: يعنون هودا، عليه السلام، { إلا بشر مثلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs call those who obey a human like themselves losers, meaning incapable or feeble.
rows.anchor: يعنى لعجزة، مثلها فى يوسف عليه السلام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud's promise is that they will be brought out of the earth alive after death.
rows.anchor: { أيعدكم } هود { أنكم إذا متم وكنتم ترابا وعظاما أنكم مخرجون } [آية: 35] من الأرض أحياء بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that the promise is old, worn-out talk no longer remembered.
rows.anchor: { هيهات هيهات لما توعدون } [آية: 36] يقول: هذا حديث قد درس، فلا يذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim is that one generation dies and others born from their descendants live, in an endless cycle.
rows.anchor: { إن هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا نموت ونحيا } يعنى نموت نحن ويحيا آخرون من أصلابنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They deny being resurrected after death; Muqatil notes a parallel in Surat al-Jathiya.
rows.anchor: { وما نحن بمبعوثين } [آية: 37] بعد الموت مثلها فى الجاثية
